input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale:
Section 28.1 selects Singapore law with exclusive Singapore courts — the Vendor-friendly foreign forum that sits outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and in walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 28.2, which confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County. The minimal fix conforms 28.1 to the preferred position (New York law) and defers venue to Section 28.2, resolving the internal conflict. The Section 28.3 executive-escalation step and the carve-out for interim injunctive relief are acceptable and left intact.</rationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.95

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore courts with New York law and the New York County courts already named in Section 28.2.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Singapore to New York and pointed venue to the New York County courts, since our playbook requires New York (or Delaware, California, or England and Wales) law and courts rather than a foreign forum. This also removes the direct conflict with Section 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts.

ops.oldText: governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and jurisdiction and venue are as set out in Section 28.2.
